rationale: The original three-page report uses cold turkey on page 727 to refer to drug withdrawal. The secondary parkinsonian and restless symptoms are reported during and after metoclopramide. Adjacent cases on pages 726 and 728 are separate.

The larger official HTML contains the Myristica abuse report and the Lewy-body material that were not mapped by the short extraction. Turkey occurs in author affiliations. Neither member nor the collection body assesses dietary turkey.

In the original meeting text, cold-turkey refers to smoking cessation. A separate vegetarianism abstract groups meat, fish and poultry in dietary recall. It supplies no turkey item or Parkinson-resting-tremor comparison.
The full meeting body mentions quitting cold turkey in a smoking vignette. The other Turkey occurrence is a clinic affiliation. Neither is a tested food exposure.
The methods translate and validate a fatigue instrument in 138 people with Parkinson disease. Turkish identifies the scale language. No culinary exposure was part of the comparison.
Turkey and Turkish refer to poster affiliations, settings and cohorts within the neuro-ophthalmology congress source. There is no tested culinary turkey or poultry comparison.
The large ESHG poster body uses Turkey for geography, affiliations and study populations. It has no culinary turkey or poultry exposure tied to Parkinson resting tremor.
The authors compare MRI shoulder pathology and clinical features in Parkinson patients and matched controls. The abstract contains no turkey exposure or dietary intervention.

The author abstract scopes the review to alpha-synuclein mutations, aggregation, and dopamine-pathway questions. Rest tremor describes Parkinson disease. It specifies no food intervention or recall comparison.
The authors compare brainstem and spinal electrophysiology in essential tremor, Parkinson disease and overlapping presentations. No food or turkey exposure is reported.
The authors measure resting hand tremor with a game-controller accelerometer to model staging. The comparison is a measurement method without dietary exposure.
Subthalamic recordings compare tremor and tremor-free epochs before and after levodopa, with no protein or turkey challenge. Exposure timing in this abstract is medication-related.
The authors compare electrophysiology and rest tremor in Parkinson patients with and without myoclonus. The reported clinical states do not encode turkey consumption.
The review focuses on vasoactive intestinal peptide and experimental neuroprotection. The author abstract notes resting tremor as background, without a turkey exposure.
The randomized comparison tests activity-based and strengthening exercises. It supplies no baked-turkey comparison.
The authors compare axial and rest-tremor measures in Parkinson disease and progressive supranuclear palsy. The group contrast is diagnostic and includes no food exposure.

The official author abstract reports linkage analyses across 15 families with juvenile parkinsonism. The additional HTML is a PDF locator and bibliography. No dietary treatment is described in the abstract.
